question_content:
The data 680, 680, 700, 720, 720 are:
A. Unimodal at 700
B. Bimodal at 680 and 720
C. Multimodal with three modes
D. Without any mode

For x̄ to be a good estimate of μ, the sample should be:
A. Truly random
B. Large but biased
C. Conveniently chosen
D. Evenly spaced in time

Which is a statistic?
A. Population mean μ
B. Sample mean x̄
C. Population median
D. Population mode

Which measure is generally better when there are outliers?
A. Mean
B. Median
C. Mode
D. Range
The mode is the ___ value.

From Professor Blount’s grouped test scores, the best estimate of the class mean is about:
A. 72.00
B. 76.86
C. 83.50
D. 89.50

The mean of a frequency table is computed as:
A. Sum of midpoints divided by number of intervals
B. Sum of f×m divided by sum of f
C. Largest midpoint
D. Sum of frequencies

If n = 100, the median occurs between which ordered positions?
A. 49th and 50th
B. 50th and 51st
C. 51st and 52nd
D. 100th and 101st

The Law of Large Numbers says that as sample size grows, x̄ tends to:
A. Equal the sample median
B. Get closer to μ
C. Get farther from μ
D. Become bimodal
The sample mean is represented by ___.

Which measure can be used with qualitative data (for example, colors)?
A. mode
B. mean
C. median
D. midpoint
The median is generally a better measure of center when there are extreme values or ___.

What is the midpoint of the interval 68.5–74.5?
A. 71.5
B. 68.5
C. 74.5
D. 72.5
The midpoint of an interval equals (lower boundary + upper boundary) divided by ___.

Why is the mean from a grouped frequency table only an estimate?
A. Because the individual data values are unknown; only intervals and frequencies are given.
B. Because the median is not available.
C. Because the mode is always larger than the mean.
D. Because the sample is not random.
The population mean is represented by the Greek letter ___.

What does μ represent?
A. The arithmetic mean of an entire population.
B. The median of a sample.
C. The mode of grouped data.
D. The midpoint of the middle interval.

Which term means the sum of all data values divided by the number of values?
A. arithmetic mean (average)
B. median
C. mode
D. midpoint of an interval

Which calculation finds the mean when values have frequencies?
A. Sum of (value × frequency) divided by total number of data values.
B. Sum of frequencies divided by number of distinct values.
C. Median of the distinct values.
D. Most frequent value only.
The arithmetic mean is found by adding all data values and dividing by the number of values; it is commonly called the ___.

Which measure of center is less affected by outliers?
A. Mean
B. Median
C. Both equally
D. Neither

For the sample 10, 12, 8, what is x̄?
A. 9
B. 10
C. 10.5
D. 12

Which statement is correct?
A. x̄ summarizes a sample; μ summarizes an entire population.
B. μ summarizes a sample; x̄ summarizes an entire population.
C. x̄ and μ summarize the same scope of data.
D. x̄ and μ are different symbols for the same quantity in the same data set.

Given values 2 (freq 3), 5 (freq 1), and 9 (freq 2), what is the mean?
A. 4.83
B. 5.50
C. 7.00
D. 29.00

Which measure is more robust to outliers?
A. Median
B. Mean
C. Both equally robust
D. Neither is a measure of center

Which statement correctly differentiates location and value of the median?
A. The median’s location is a position index given by (n + 1) / 2; the median’s value is the data value at that position (or the average of the two middle values for even n).
B. The median’s location always equals the median’s value.
C. The median’s location is the same as the arithmetic mean.
D. The median’s value is always (n + 1) / 2.

What are the mode(s) of the data set 1, 1, 2, 2, 3?
A. 1
B. 2
C. 1 and 2
D. No mode

A frequency table has intervals with frequencies: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 5, 20–29: 2. How many data values are represented in total?
A. 8
B. 9
C. 10
D. 11

What is the midpoint of the class interval 10–14?
A. 11
B. 12
C. 13
D. 12.5

Given intervals and frequencies: 0–10 (f=2), 10–20 (f=1). Using midpoints, what is the estimated mean Σ(fm)/Σf?
A. 5.00
B. 8.33
C. 10.00
D. 15.00

When estimating the mean from a grouped frequency table, each class is represented by its:
A. Lower boundary
B. Upper boundary
C. Midpoint
D. Class width

A data set with two modes is called:
A. Unimodal
B. Bimodal
C. Multimodal
D. Symmetric

Which measure of center is better when there are extreme values?
A. Mean
B. Median
C. Mode
D. Range

Which symbol represents the population mean?
A. x̄
B. μ
C. M
D. n

In the AIDS drug example with 40 values, what is the median?
A. 23.6
B. 24
C. 20.5
D. 40

Which symbol represents the sample mean?
A. x̄
B. μ
C. M
D. n

In a town with one $5,000,000 earner and 49 earners of $30,000, which is the better measure of center?
A. Mean
B. Median
C. Mode
D. Range

Which measure can be calculated for qualitative data?
A. Mean
B. Median
C. Mode
D. Midpoint

The expression (n + 1) / 2 gives the:
A. Mean
B. Value of the median
C. Location of the median
D. Mode
